newsitem.title: TAIWAN: FORECAST-Taiwan May industry output seen up slowly.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Taiwan May industry output seen up slowly.

text.p: A Reuters poll of Taiwan economists on Thursday projected an average 4.266 percent rise of Taiwan's industrial output in May, a relatively slow upturn reflecting a high year-on-year comparative base.
The official figures were due to be released by the economics ministry at around 0230 GMT on June 21.
In April, Taiwan's industrial output rose 6.12 percent year-on-year. The indicator had risen an average of 5.94 percent year-on-year in January-April.

Economists attributed the forecasts for relatively slow growth partly to a comparatively high base in May 1996, when the industrial output index stood at 125.42 -- even though that level actually reflected a 1.79 percent year-on-year decline due to overall poor performance in 1996.
They pointed to sluggish property market sales in May 1997 amid a series of mass protests demanding a cabinet reshuffle and improvement of social order.

"Local demand, especially in the construction sector, likely slowed due to political uncertainties triggered by people's demand for a cabinet reshuffle in May," said Nomura Securities analyst Amy Huang.

Economists said they expected the industrial output growth in coming months to be slower than the 5.94 percent average in the first four months because a domestic recovery, though still unfolding, was doing so more slowly than hoped.

"Unless exports in the second half turn much stronger, second half industrial output growth will be slower than the average in the first four months," said Grand Cathay Securities vice-president Terry Chen.
